official.deadline_note: There is no single MOE deadline. Applicants first apply for admission to a participating university - NCKU's 2026 Fall admission round ran mid-December 2025 to mid-March 2026 - then, after admission, submit the scholarship application and Lecturer Certificate by the deadline the university sets (NCKU set Wednesday 23 September 2026 for AY2026/27). African-route applicants may also apply for Spring admission, for which NCKU's application window was July to September 2026.
official.application_cycle: AY2026/27 (announcement dated 2026.08); MOE announces recipients around late October for the Fall intake and late April for the African Spring intake
official.status_note: The AY2026/27 round at NCKU closed its scholarship document stage on 23 September 2026 and is now at the MOE review stage, with recipient lists announced around late October for Fall entry. The programme runs on an annual cycle tied to each participating university's admission rounds, so the next cycle opens with the university's next admission window.
official.tuition_coverage_note: NCKU publishes: 'The Elite scholarship is issued by MOE, which is used as funding for your tuition fee and credit fee, and the remaining amount will be used as a monthly stipend to support your study and living in NCKU.' The MOE guidelines list permitted uses of the stipend as tuition and miscellaneous fees, thesis supervision, insurance, accommodations, internet use and living allowance. Taipei Tech by contrast pays tuition out of the award and tops up nothing, and TNUA states students 'will need to pay tuition fee and credit fee' - the tuition treatment is set by each participating university.
benefits: Monthly award of NT$25,000 issued by MOE - NTD 300,000 or approx. USD 10,000 per year at NCKU's approx. 30:1 exchange rate note.
The award is used as funding for tuition fee and credit fee, and the remaining amount is used as a monthly stipend to support study and living at the university.
Stipends may be used to cover tuition and miscellaneous fees, thesis supervision, insurance, accommodations, internet use and living allowance.
Duration of up to 3 years in doctoral programmes and 2 years in master's programmes, reviewed annually; enrolment procedures must be completed every semester to keep the scholarship continuous.
One hundred students per academic year over three academic years may be awarded this scholarship, a total of three hundred students.
eligibility: Doctoral/Master's degree-seeking applicants who are currently university lecturers or professors (lecturer level or above) in an eligible country.

South and Southeast Asian countries (Fall admission): Indonesia, Philippines, Thailand, Vietnam, India, Malaysia, Singapore, Brunei, Myanmar, Cambodia, Laos, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Nepal, Sri Lanka and Bhutan.

All African countries (Fall or Spring admission): either current university lecturers or professors with an up-to-date Lecturer Certificate, or 3 years (or above) of university researcher experience with research publications or papers.
Must hold the lecturer position at a public or private higher education institution in the eligible country, with the teaching position on hold because of the studies.
Must provide an up-to-date Lecturer Certificate (English version); the African researcher route requires an Employment Certificate (English version) plus research publications.
Must not hold Taiwan (R.O.C.) nationality or the status of an overseas Chinese student.

Must not be enrolled in, or have retained admission to, a university in Taiwan (this restriction does not apply to students on course to graduate who will be pursuing their next degree, provided they are still lecturers from South or Southeast Asian countries).
Must not have previously studied in Taiwan for a degree at the same level.
Must not be an exchange student or dual-degree student through a partnership agreement with an institution overseas.
Must not have already received stipends through this programme for more than three years.
Must not have been awarded another form of financial assistance or scholarship from a Taiwan (R.O.C.) government agency, or from a foreign government, to support studies.
Participating schools must offer full English-taught programmes in which all courses are taught in English, rather than just enough English courses to meet graduation credits.
requirements: Hold a current university lecturer, assistant professor or professor post at a higher education institution in an eligible country, with the post on hold because of the studies.
Apply to a participating university and choose a full English-taught programme (NCKU requires applicants to choose its Full English Taught Programs).
Provide an up-to-date Lecturer Certificate (English version); African researcher-route applicants provide an Employment Certificate (English version) and research publications or papers.
Complete the university's registration and tuition payment procedures during the tuition payment period.
Complete enrolment procedures every semester to receive the two/three-year continuous scholarship.
Apply for renewal each year, subject to review; the guidelines require a minimum average of 80 in the previous academic year to continue.
documents: African researcher route: Employment Certificate (English version) plus research publications or papers
University admission application submitted through the participating university's international student admissions system
MOE-Elite scholarship application form via the link provided by the university's Office of International Affairs after admission (NCKU used an online form for AY2026/27)
selection_criteria: The admission application is evaluated by the department; the university's Office of International Affairs provides the list of candidates to the MOE for final reviewing and approval.
Priority is given to applicants enrolling in doctoral programmes.
Quota is allocated by the MOE - one hundred students per academic year - so a waitlist is possible.
coverage: Total award of NT$25,000 per month (NT$300,000 per year) issued by MOE.
Tuition fee and credit fee are funded out of the total award; the remaining amount is paid as a monthly stipend to support study and living.
Stipends may be used for tuition and miscellaneous fees, thesis supervision, insurance, accommodations, internet use and living allowance.

Remaining stipends may not be retained or deferred; the scholarship is suspended while the student is outside Taiwan, and a student who departs after the fifteenth day of a month need not return that month's stipend.
application_method: Complete and submit the admission application to the participating university, choosing a full English-taught programme.
After the admission results, candidates who received admission finish registration with the Registrar Division.
Submit the MOE-Elite scholarship application with the up-to-date Lecturer Certificate by the deadline stated by the university (NCKU: 23 September 2026 for AY2026/27).

The university's Office of International Affairs provides the candidate list to the MOE, which reviews and determines the awards and announces recipients (around late October for Fall, late April for the African Spring intake).
Awardees complete enrolment procedures every semester and apply for annual renewal, subject to review.
official.application_route: Apply for admission to a participating university's full English-taught graduate programme, then after admission submit the MOE-Elite application and Lecturer Certificate by the university's stated deadline; the university forwards candidates to the MOE for final approval.
official.study_mode: Full-time degree study at a participating university (Taipei Tech specifies newly admitted full-time PhD students; NCKU requires its Full English Taught Programs)
official.citizenship_residency: Citizens of eligible South, Southeast Asian or African countries whose teaching post is held at a public or private higher education institution in that country; holders of Taiwan (R.O.C.) nationality or overseas Chinese student status are excluded.
official.international_eligibility: International applicants only - the programme exists to bring lecturers from South and Southeast Asian and African countries to Taiwan.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: No subject restriction is published, but the applicant must be admitted to a participating university's full English-taught programme, and priority is given to doctoral study. Participating universities must offer full English-taught programmes and have enrolled at least twenty international students in graduate programmes in the previous academic year.
official.research_requirement: No research proposal is required for the lecturer route. The African researcher route requires 3 years or above of university researcher experience with research publications or papers.
official.duration: Up to 2 years for a master's programme and up to 3 years for a doctoral programme, reviewed annually; enrolment procedures must be completed every semester for the continuous award. Some universities run their own version for longer - Taipei Tech funds up to 4 years for newly admitted PhD students.
official.description: The MOE Elite Scholarship Program was created by Taiwan's Ministry of Education, under the New Southbound Policy Work Plan announced by the Executive Yuan in December 2016, to encourage university lecturers from South and Southeast Asian and African countries to pursue master's or doctoral degrees in Taiwan, with priority given to doctoral programmes. Each awardee receives a monthly award of NT$25,000 (NT$300,000 per year), from which tuition and credit fees are funded, with the remainder paid as a monthly stipend to support study and living. It is administered through participating universities, which admit the applicant and forward the case to the MOE for final approval.
official.program_type: Government graduate scholarship for university lecturers from South, Southeast Asia and Africa to study in Taiwan (MOE New Southbound Policy Talent Development Program)

travel_coverage - no airfare or travel benefit is published under this programme
the exact net in-pocket stipend at NCKU (only Taipei Tech publishes a post-tuition split)
exact dates of the next admission cycle beyond the published AY2026/27 windows
verification.notes: Amount, duration, eligibility, exclusions, application route and the 23 September 2026 AY2026/27 deadline were taken from NCKU OIA's official scholarship page and its AY2026/27 announcement PDF; stipend-use, termination and quota wording from the MOE guidelines as published by National Pingtung University; the programme does not appear on the MOE English scholarships list, which carries only the Taiwan Scholarship, HES, UMAP, STRA and MOE APEC schemes.

applicant_utility.summary: Budget on the money that actually reaches your account, not the headline NT$25,000: MOE issues the total award and the university deducts tuition and credit fees first, so your usable stipend is only the remainder, which at Taipei Tech is about NT$14,000 a month in years 1-3. The real bottleneck is MOE quota approval, not admission - universities nominate admitted candidates and the ministry approves a capped 100 places per academic year, so strong admission alone does not secure the award. Start the paperwork early: an up-to-date English Lecturer Certificate and written confirmation that your teaching post is on hold are hard prerequisites that many applicants only discover after admission. Holding any other Taiwan government scholarship or grant disqualifies you outright, so choose between this and other funding before you apply.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Serving university lecturers, assistant professors and professors from South/Southeast Asia or Africa who can put their post on hold, hold a current English Lecturer Certificate, and want a funded full English-taught master's or PhD in Taiwan.
application_readiness_checklist: Request an up-to-date Lecturer Certificate in English (or, for the African researcher route, an Employment Certificate plus publication list) well before the university's post-admission deadline.
Get written confirmation from your institution that your teaching position will be placed on hold for the whole study period.
Identify participating universities whose full English-taught programmes actually cover all courses in English, not just enough English credits.
Declare any other Taiwan government or foreign government funding and decide which single award you will keep.
Complete the university's registration and tuition payment steps promptly - missing them interrupts the award.
common_rejection_risks: Assuming the NT$25,000 is disposable income when tuition and credit fees are deducted from it first.
Holding any other Taiwan government scholarship or grant, which the MOE guidelines make an automatic exclusion.

Being currently enrolled at, or holding retained admission to, a Taiwanese university when applying (only graduating students moving up a level are exempted, and only if still lecturers from eligible countries).
Losing the award after admission by taking a leave of absence, receiving a demerit, failing the school's standards, or swapping into an exchange or dual-degree track.
Letting the average mark slip - renewal requires a minimum average of 80 in the previous academic year under the published guidelines.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Airfare to and from Taiwan, any amount of tuition above what the award covers at universities that do not fully fund it, dependants' costs, and any expense beyond the post-tuition stipend remainder; non-retained stipends cannot be saved or deferred for later months.
document_audit: The Lecturer Certificate must be the English version and current - expired or local-language-only certificates stall the file at the university stage.
African researcher-route applicants must supply BOTH the Employment Certificate and actual publications, not a publication promise.
Because the scholarship application only opens after admission, keep certificate scans ready months before admission results land.
alerts: Two-stage timing: the admission window and the scholarship document deadline are separate - NCKU's AY2026/27 admission round closed mid-March 2026 while its scholarship document deadline was 23 September 2026.
MOE quota means a waitlist is normal; candidates later approved from the waitlist must repay stipends already disbursed before the award can be confirmed.
Remaining stipends cannot be retained or deferred, and leaving Taiwan suspends the scholarship - plan fieldwork or home visits around semesters.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Admission application to the university (full English-taught programme), then post-admission registration plus the MOE-Elite form and Lecturer Certificate upload, then university nomination to MOE and final MOE approval.

official.deadline_note: Applications for research in Taiwan in the following year must arrive at the host institution no later than 30 September each year (date of receipt). The 30 September 2026 deadline covered research in 2027; applications received by it are now with host institutions, which must forward their supported files with a one-page Chinese research summary to the MOE by 15 November the same year, and MOE sends decision copies to ROC embassies/missions by 31 January of the next year.
official.application_cycle: Annual, aligned with Taiwan's fiscal year; research is in principle undertaken between 1 March and 31 December of the year following the 30 September deadline
official.status_note: Standing annual award with roughly 20 awards available each fiscal year, the actual number depending on the annual budget. The page was last updated 8 October 2026 and the Directions governing it are the April 2015 revision effective since 2012.
benefits: A monthly research allowance of NTD $25,000 for a Ph.D. student.
A monthly research allowance of NTD $40,000 for a postdoctoral fellow.

An economy class round-trip airfare for the most direct route between the recipient's place of residence and Taiwan, Penghu, Kinmen or Matsu, with the maximum subsidy set by MOE regulations and the recipient responsible for any expense above the set maximum.
A short-term research stay of between 2 and 6 months in Taiwan, in principle between 1 March and 31 December of the fiscal year.
eligibility: Be a Ph.D. student currently undertaking a doctorate programme at an overseas government approved and registered public or private university or tertiary college; or

be a postdoctoral research fellow awarded a Ph.D. by any government approved and registered public or private university or tertiary college, in Taiwan or overseas, who is now undertaking a research project at an overseas university, tertiary college, or institution of higher education (priority is given to scholars who have completed a dissertation, book/s and/or other publication/s).
Not hold an R.O.C. (Taiwanese) passport.
Not be currently visiting, residing, studying (including undertaking an internship), teaching, or undertaking research activity in Taiwan at the time of application.
Not be currently receiving other financial assistance from a government agency or an educational institution in Taiwan to undertake a research project.

Not be an exchange student under any academic co-operation agreement signed between a university or tertiary college in Taiwan and an overseas university or college during the proposed research period in Taiwan.
Not have received an STRA award within the last 5 years.
Scholars from mainland China, Hong Kong and Macao are excluded.
requirements: The research topic must be related to Taiwan in a humanities discipline, the social sciences, a culture and/or arts field, and/or related comparative research.

The application must be submitted to a host institution in Taiwan - a university or tertiary college, or a research organization affiliated with the MOE such as the Center for Chinese Studies or the National Academy for Educational Research - at which the applicant would like to undertake research.
The short-term research period must be between 2 and 6 months, aligned with the fiscal year and in principle undertaken between 1 March and 31 December.

The recipient must take out accident and medical insurance effective for the full period of the research stay in Taiwan, and must register for Taiwan's National Health Insurance if they acquire an ARC and become eligible.
documents: Three copies of the STRA Application Form (appendix 1 of the Directions)
Postdoctoral fellow: a photocopy of the Ph.D. certificate; Ph.D. student: certification of current enrolment, transcripts, and documentary evidence of the academic programmes completed

At least two letters of recommendation - one from a senior official of the institution where the applicant currently works or studies (e.g. president, vice-chancellor, institute director, college dean, department head or research institute head), and one from a teaching scholar or expert in the applicant's field; Ph.D. students must also submit certification of current enrolment
A one-page A4 Chinese summary of the research proposal, prepared with the host institution's assistance before submission to the MOE
selection_criteria: The host institution undertakes the initial review and only supported proposals are forwarded to the MOE by 15 November.

An MOE selection panel of three to five people - MOE officials and scholars and/or experts in the applicants' fields - selects recipients; only applicants who receive at least 70 points out of 100 from each panellist may be selected.

Scoring: the applicant's potential, outstanding personal performance and ability to carry out the proposal (30%); the applicant's language ability and the academic reputation of the host research institution and its appropriateness for the proposal (30%); the overall quality and comprehensiveness of the research proposal - topic, structure, methodology and analysis - its feasibility, and the project's importance to future development of the applicant's home country and Taiwan (40%).
coverage: Monthly research allowance: NTD $25,000 for a Ph.D. student and NTD $40,000 for a postdoctoral fellow, transferred on the tenth of each month beginning from the month after the recipient arrives in Taiwan.

Economy class round-trip airfare for the most direct route between the place of residence and Taiwan, Penghu, Kinmen or Matsu; maximum subsidy amounts are set by MOE regulations and the recipient pays any excess.
Airfare reimbursement requires evidence of the plane ticket cost and a boarding pass or flight ticket stub, submitted with a written request including a receipt.
No tuition fee or degree-award funding is provided - the MOE does not provide recipients housing or a research room either.

A Research Project Report (appendix 2 format, noting research results such as papers or published material) and a funds income and expenditure statement are due to the MOE within one month of completing the research.
application_method: Identify a host institution in Taiwan - a university, tertiary college, or MOE-affiliated research organization such as the Center for Chinese Studies or the National Academy for Educational Research - and secure its agreement to host the research.

Prepare the application form, qualification documents, transcripts and at least two recommendation letters and lodge them with the host institution so that everything arrives by 30 September (date of receipt).
The host institution reviews the application; if it supports the proposal it helps prepare the one-page A4 Chinese research summary and submits it with all other documents to the MOE by 15 November.

The MOE convenes its selection panel and notifies host institutions of the decisions, which then notify applicants; the MOE also sends a copy of each decision to the ROC embassy or diplomatic mission in the applicant's home country or place of residence by 31 January of the next year.

After arrival in Taiwan, the host institution requests appropriation of the research subsidy; the monthly allowance is paid from the month after arrival, and airfare is reimbursed against ticket evidence and boarding pass.
official.application_route: Apply directly to a chosen Taiwanese host institution (university, tertiary college or MOE-affiliated research organization) so the complete file arrives by 30 September; the host reviews, forwards supported applications to the MOE by 15 November, and notifies the outcome.
official.study_mode: Short-term research stay of 2 to 6 months (non-degree research visit)
official.citizenship_residency: Open to international scholars who do not hold an R.O.C. (Taiwanese) passport; scholars from mainland China, Hong Kong and Macao are excluded. Applicants must not be currently visiting, residing, studying, interning, teaching or researching in Taiwan.
official.international_eligibility: International PhD students and postdoctoral fellows based at overseas institutions only.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: The research topic must relate to Taiwan in a humanities discipline, the social sciences, a culture and/or arts field, and/or related comparative research. Research must be hosted by a Taiwanese university, tertiary college or an MOE-affiliated research organization such as the Center for Chinese Studies or the National Academy for Educational Research.
official.research_requirement: A research proposal on a Taiwan-related topic in humanities, social sciences, culture and/or arts, or related comparative research is required; the host institution prepares a one-page A4 Chinese summary for the MOE, and priority is given to applicants who have completed a dissertation, book/s and/or other publication/s.
official.duration: Between 2 and 6 months of research in Taiwan, aligned with the fiscal year and in principle undertaken between 1 March and 31 December of the year after application.
official.description: The Ministry of Education Short Term Research Awards (STRA) are offered to international scholars - excluding those from mainland China, Hong Kong and Macao - to encourage them to undertake short-term research in Taiwan, to increase their understanding of Taiwan's culture and society, and to promote mutual understanding and interaction between Taiwan and the international community. Awards run for 2 to 6 months, provide a monthly research allowance of NTD $25,000 for PhD students or NTD $40,000 for postdoctoral fellows plus economy-class round-trip airfare, and are applied for through a Taiwanese host institution by 30 September each year.
official.program_type: Short-term research grant (MOE subsidy for international PhD students and postdoctoral fellows)

verification.notes: Amounts, allowances, eligibility, topic area, the 30 September deadline and the STRA overview were taken from the MOE's own Short Term Research Award page; documents, selection scoring, payment schedule, insurance rules and post-award obligations from the MOE Laws and Regulations Retrieval System text of the Directions Governing MOE Subsidies for Short Term Research Awards (revised 10 April 2015).

applicant_utility.summary: Treat the host institution as the real gatekeeper: your file must physically arrive there by 30 September, and only files the host supports reach the MOE by 15 November, so contact potential hosts in Taiwan by mid-year and agree the research plan before the summer. Build the application around the panel's scoring - every one of the three to five panellists must give you at least 70 out of 100, weighting proposal quality, feasibility and Taiwan relevance at 40%. Budget the stay knowing the MOE provides no housing or research room and that the monthly allowance (NTD 25,000 as a PhD student, NTD 40,000 as a postdoc) starts only in the month after you arrive. Arrange accident and medical insurance for the entire stay before departure, because the first payment and airfare reimbursement are withheld while you are uninsured.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Overseas PhD students and postdoctoral fellows with a Taiwan-related humanities, social-science or arts/comparative research project, publications or a completed dissertation, and a willing Taiwanese host department.
application_readiness_checklist: Shortlist host universities or MOE-affiliated bodies (Center for Chinese Studies, National Academy for Educational Research) and secure a host contact months before September.
Confirm your own enrolment status proof as a PhD student, or your PhD certificate as a postdoc, plus full transcripts.
Line up the two required referees - one senior official from your home institution and one academic expert in your field - and give them the draft early.
Draft a Taiwan-focused proposal with concrete methodology and sources in Taiwanese archives or institutions, since proposal quality carries 40% of the score.
Buy accident and medical insurance covering the whole 2-6 month stay before flying, and keep the flight ticket and boarding pass for reimbursement.
common_rejection_risks: Missing the host's internal cut-off - only supported files leave the host by 15 November, so a 30 September postmark is not enough if the host needs review time.
A single panellist scoring below 70 eliminates the applicant regardless of the average.
Any current presence in Taiwan (visiting, studying, interning, teaching or researching) at application time voids eligibility.
Holding other Taiwanese government or institutional research funding during the proposed period.
A prior STRA award within the last 5 years, which is an automatic bar.
Leaving Taiwan mid-stay without host permission - an overseas stay over ten days forfeits one month's subsidy permanently.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Accommodation and any research-room or workspace costs (the MOE provides neither), any airfare above the maximum economy subsidy on the most direct route, National Health Insurance premiums once an ARC is held, visa and living costs in the first month before the allowance starts, and any paid work, which recipients may not undertake.
document_audit: Three paper copies of the application form are required - do not send a single electronic file.
PhD students must submit BOTH enrolment certification and transcripts plus evidence of completed programmes; postdocs submit the PhD certificate photocopy.
The Chinese one-page summary is drafted with the host's help - a weak or machine-translated summary undermines the 40% proposal score.
Airfare reimbursement needs the actual ticket cost evidence plus the boarding pass or stub submitted after arrival, not before.
alerts: Timing trap: research in the following year requires arrival at the host by 30 September of the current year, with the MOE decision only confirmed by 31 January - do not resign, rent or book flights before the decision.
The award follows the fiscal year, with research in principle between 1 March and 31 December, so a late-year start compresses the 2-6 month stay.
Recipients may not accept any other award or subsidy from a government agency or academic institution during the Taiwan stay, and false documents trigger repayment of everything received.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: File lodged with the chosen Taiwanese host institution by 30 September, host review and supported submission to the MOE by 15 November with a Chinese one-page summary, MOE panel selection, notification via the host and ROC missions by 31 January, then payment through the host from the month after arrival.
